newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African bond market ended a topsey-turvey day in slightly weaker territory as the market struggled for direction after healthy buying on Monday.
Bond yields swung from highs of around 14.96 percent to lows near 14.86 percent on the back of a mixture of good buying and selling, traders said.
"It's been like a washing machine: the market was thrown around all over the place," a dealer noted.
He said the market had looked for consolidation after moving nearly 40 basis points lower over the last five days but instead players accumulated stock during the day.

Another dealer said the day had been characterised by good two-way flows and he still expected yields to consolidate or move a touch higher ahead of the release of August CPI data at 0900 GMT on Thursday, which is expected to come in higher on a year-on-year basis.
Traders said buying and selling interest had come from all quarters with foreigners seen eyeing stock during the morning session.
At 1416 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was at 14.930 percent from 14.90 percent overnight.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 38.57 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 266.98 million rand on Friday. Nominal cumulative volumes were 5.11 billion rand on Monday after 8.85 billion rand on Friday.
The rand ended one of its sleepiest days in a long time virtually unchanged from its previous closing levels.
At 1416 GMT it was at 4.4840/4890 on the dollar from 4.4835/4885 late on Monday.
Dealers said the unit was seen trading sideways amid an absence of fresh news but sentiment remained positive.

"The rand has been doing fairly well in recent weeks. Sentiment is better and we are seeing a period of relative stability which has squeezed speculators out of their positions," a senior trader noted.

He said there was still natural importer demand at all levels and while many players were calling the market lower to around the 4.46/45 levels in the short-term, some were sceptical due to resistance that the unit has in the past met at the 4.48 level.
Against the crosses, the currency was last trading at 6.9704/9804 against sterling from 6.9751/9929 late on Monday and at 0.3374/3379 marks from 0.3369/3374 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent while 90-day BAs were also unchanged at between 15.20 to 15.40 percent from 15.20 to 15.45 percent.
The Reserve Bank put the daily shortage at below the key eight billion mark for the second day running, to be quoted at 7.931 billion rand on Monday from 7.484 billion rand on Saturday.
